messages:
kim: Heads up — after the routing weight change to favor eu-pool, the dashboard p99 for text.generate jumped ~120ms but p50 stayed flat. screenshot: https://redwood.screenshot/abc123 :thinking_face:
ajay: hmm, is that p99 measured in ms or 'tokens' bucket?
kim: ms. The dashboard label says 'latency (ms) p99' but the numbers look suspiciously aligned with tokenization boundaries (e.g. 64/128/256).
sloane: can you paste the raw query from the console? sometimes the rollup path does histogram quantile vs raw quantile and interpolation looks funky.
kim: sure — from the console: ```sql
SELECT quantile(0.99)(lat_ms) AS p99_ms, count()
FROM endpoint_traces
WHERE endpoint = 'text.generate' AND env = 'prod' AND region = 'us-west'
    AND timestamp >= now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY route_id
```
ajay: ok — that is quantile over raw lat_ms. the dashboard rollup, though, may be merging t-digests from shards with linear interpolation. if shard samples are low, p99 can snap to a boundary.
oliver: also check if we surface post-tokenization or pre-tokenization latency. tokenization step sometimes adds spikes at boundary sizes. could be correlated with batch/seq length after route shift.
sloane: quick check: what's sample_count for the affected route? low N amplifies interpolation artifacts.
kim: sample counts: route A (old primary): 12k, route B (eu-pool): 4200. p99 jump mostly in route B.
ajay: that aligns. two things to verify: 1) rollup path (merging tdigests vs recomputing from raw samples), 2) whether we convert to ms after aggregation rounding to nearest 1ms (could snap values).
sloane: also the console legend shows p99 rounded to integers — UI rounding + tooltip may hide fractional differences.
kim: @oliver can you confirm whether routing changed weights at 17:23? deploy-bot shows canary finished at 17:20.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout for route-weight-tweak completed at 2025-10-17T17:20:03Z. :white_check_mark:
oliver: yep, that was the change. I think the eu pool packetization leads to bigger seq lengths for some customers, so a genuine tail effect is plausible.
ajay: for next steps: (a) run a raw-sample quantile on the eu pool only (no rollups), (b) compare histogram buckets (count per latency bin) to see if there's a discrete mass at boundaries, (c) add a temporary debug tag to traces to mark tokenization step timings.
sloane: I'll add a small dashboard card that shows sample_count and raw p99 side-by-side for the top 5 routes.
kim: sounds good. if (a) shows no jump, it's a rollup/interpolation bug. if (a) shows jump, we need to investigate batching/tokenization.
oliver: I'll run (a) now and post results shortly.
kim: thanks — appreciate the fast triage :thumbsup:
kim: follow-up (17:35) — oliver posted raw p99 for eu-pool: 9.8ms -> 134ms (wow). attached: small CSV. looks real. we should alert product to potential perf regression for eu routing.
sloane: raising an incident-lite and adding to the routing-rollback playbook. I'll open a ticket with logs + sample histograms.
kim: filing ticket now. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian/browse/RINF-3211 — will add the CSV and screenshots.
ajay: also queue an eval to run small seq-length-specific stress tests on eu pool to confirm.
kim: will do. thanks everyone.
